object: SNCA

subject: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009)
object: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) found that PD risk alleles at the MAPT locus were in LD with the H1 haplotype (r2 = 0.761 with rs393152). Expression analysis in 133 human frontal cortex samples showed that the risk allele of rs393152 was associated with higher MAPT expression and lower LRRC37A expression.

subject: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009)
object: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) replicated in Europeans a locus on chromosome 1q32 found in a Japanese GWAS, designated PARK16 (rs823128, OR = 0.66, combined P = 7.29 x 10(-8); replication cohort of 2,816 cases and 3,401 controls). The locus spans SNORA72, NUCKS1, RAB7L1, SLC41A1, and PM20D1. They failed to replicate the 4p15 (BST1) signal from the Japanese study, possibly owing to low minor allele frequency in Caucasians.

subject: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009)
object: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) provided supporting evidence that common variation around LRRK2 modulates PD risk: rs1491923, 0.17 Mb upstream of LRRK2, gave a combined OR of 1.14 (P = 1.55 x 10(-5)), and the Asian cohort also showed association at this locus.

subject: LRRK2 rs1491923
object: LRRK2

subject: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009)
object: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) suggested population-specific genetic heterogeneity in PD, because the MAPT association was absent in the Japanese cohort, whereas SNCA association was replicated across populations.

subject: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009)
object: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) estimated that the combined population attributable risk of the identified loci was approximately 25%, and cautioned that these values should be interpreted carefully.

subject: Satake et al. (2009)
object: Satake et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study and two replication studies in a total of 2,011 Japanese patients with Parkinson disease and 18,381 controls. They identified a new susceptibility locus on chromosome 1q32 (P = 1.52 x 10(-12)) and designated it PARK16.

subject: Satake et al. (2009)
object: In the same Japanese GWAS, Satake et al. (2009) identified BST1 on chromosome 4p15 as a second new risk locus for Parkinson disease (P = 3.94 x 10(-9)).

subject: Satake et al. (2009)
object: Satake et al. (2009) found strong associations between Parkinson disease and SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)) and LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)) in Japanese individuals. Both genes are implicated in autosomal dominant forms of parkinsonism, and the authors concluded that autosomal dominant parkinsonism loci are involved in typical PD.

subject: Satake et al. (2009)
object: Satake et al. (2009) compared their results with a GWAS of individuals of European ancestry. PARK16, SNCA and LRRK2 were risk loci shared by both populations, while BST1 and MAPT showed population differences. The authors suggested that population differences contribute to genetic heterogeneity in PD.

subject: Elstner et al. (2009)
object: Elstner et al. (2009) identified an association between idiopathic PD and an intron 8 SNP in the PDXK gene, rs2010795. In a German cohort of 676 PD patients and 972 controls, the association was p = 3.2 x 10(-4) (OR 1.319; 95% CI 1.134-1.534). It was replicated in British (203 cases, 1,126 controls; p = 0.028; OR 1.3) and Italian (353 cases, 704 controls; p = 0.00252; OR 1.35) cohorts. In the combined analysis of 1,232 PD patients and 2,802 controls the p value was 1.18 x 10(-7) (OR 1.304; 95% CI 1.178-1.444). A second PDXK SNP in the 3-prime UTR, rs2070535, was also associated in the German cohort (p = 6.4 x 10(-4); OR 0.783).

subject: Elstner et al. (2009)
object: Elstner et al. (2009) carried out whole-genome expression profiling of laser-microdissected substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons from 8 PD patients and 9 controls. Four transcripts were significantly altered after Bonferroni correction: MTND2, PDXK and SRGAP3 were upregulated, and TRAPPC4 was downregulated. Upregulation of ND2 and PDXK was confirmed by real-time PCR. The mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain genes were upregulated, while 13 nuclear-encoded respiratory chain genes were downregulated.

subject: Elstner et al. (2009)
object: Elstner et al. (2009) found no association between PD and tagging SNPs in TRAPPC4. They suggested that variation in PDXK might influence PD risk by altering the amount or activity of the enzyme in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons. PDXK produces pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate, a cofactor of dopa decarboxylase.

subject: Gan-Or et al. (2010)
object: Gan-Or et al. (2010) screened 600 Ashkenazi Jewish patients with Parkinson disease for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and for 8 GBA mutations, and compared reported initial symptoms among GBA mutation carriers, LRRK2 G2019S carriers, and noncarriers. More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity; p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008) as initial symptoms, whereas more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia; p = 0.021). The authors suggested that LRRK2 and GBA mutations have distinct effects on the initial symptoms of PD.

subject: Plaitakis et al. (2010)
object: Plaitakis et al. (2010) found that a rare T1492G variant in GLUD2, an X-linked gene that encodes the brain-expressed glutamate dehydrogenase hGDH2, interacted significantly with age at PD onset in Caucasian populations. The variant results in a Ser445Ala substitution in the regulatory domain of hGDH2. Hemizygous individuals developed PD 6 to 13 years earlier than subjects with other genotypes in 2 independent Greek PD groups and 1 North American PD cohort. Female PD patients who were heterozygous for the variant did not show this effect.

subject: GLUD2 c.1492T>G / p.S445A
object: GLUD2

subject: Plaitakis et al. (2010)
object: Plaitakis et al. (2010) showed that the Ser445Ala variant hGDH2 enzyme had increased basal activity that resisted GTP inhibition but was markedly sensitive to modification by estrogens. They concluded that this gain-of-function variant hastens PD onset in hemizygous subjects, probably by damaging nigral cells through increased glutamate oxidative dehydrogenation. They suggested that the lack of effect in heterozygous females could be related to estrogen modification of the overactive enzyme.

subject: Vilariño-Güell et al. (2010)
object: Vilariño-Güell et al. (2010) studied the association of pyridoxal kinase (PDXK) with Parkinson disease.

subject: Guella et al. (2010)
object: Guella et al. (2010) found that the PDXK rs2010795 variant was not associated with Parkinson disease in an Italian population.

subject: Ballanger et al. (2010)
object: Ballanger et al. (2010) used PET with the selective serotonin 2A receptor ligand setoperone F 18 in 7 nondemented PD patients with complex visual hallucinations and 7 age-matched PD patients without hallucinations. Patients with visual hallucinations showed increased serotonin 2A receptor binding in the ventral visual pathway (bilateral inferooccipital gyrus, right fusiform gyrus, and inferotemporal cortex) and in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, medial orbitofrontal cortex, and insula. The authors suggested that serotonin 2A receptors mediate visual hallucinations in PD via the ventral visual pathway, and proposed treatment studies with selective serotonin 2A receptor antagonists.

subject: Tan et al. (2010)
object: Tan et al. (2010) analyzed 13 SNPs at GWAS-linked PD loci (PARK16, PARK8, PARK1, and BST1) in 2 case-control cohorts of 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects. They found that the PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci, but not BST1, were associated with PD. PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk, and PARK1 and PARK8 SNPs with an increased risk of PD.

subject: Tan et al. (2010)
object: Tan et al. (2010) performed a pooled analysis of their Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts, totaling 1,366 PD patients and 16,669 controls. It showed robust association with the PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci and also with BST1. The authors reported that the strength of association was similar in Chinese and Japanese subjects.

subject: Tan et al. (2010)
object: Tan et al. (2010) observed a trend toward a stronger protective effect of PARK16 SNPs in sporadic PD than in familial cases, and in older than in younger subjects.

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) performed a genome-wide association study of 2,000 Caucasian Parkinson disease patients and 1,986 controls from the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium (NGRC). They found a novel association with the HLA region on chromosome 6p21.3, with the peak at rs3129882 in intron 1 of the HLA-DRA gene (P = 2.9 x 10(-8) after adjustment for sex, age and 2 principal components). The association replicated in 2 independent datasets (meta-analysis OR 1.26, P = 1.9 x 10(-10)).

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) found that the HLA-DRA rs3129882 association was uniform across strata of family history, age at onset, sex and environmental exposures, and was particularly strong for sporadic PD (P = 5.5 x 10(-10)), late-onset PD (P = 2.4 x 10(-8)), and men (P = 1.1 x 10(-7)). There was no evidence for interaction with smoking, coffee, NSAIDs, SNCA rs356220, or MAPT rs199533.

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) confirmed associations of PD with SNCA (rs356220, P = 3.4 x 10(-11)) and MAPT (rs199533, P = 1.3 x 10(-6)) and replicated association with GAK on 4p16 (rs11248051; NGRC P = 3.1 x 10(-4); combined with Pankratz et al. data OR 1.46, P = 3.2 x 10(-9)). They did not replicate PARK16; 2 of 6 BST1 SNPs and 3 LRRK2 SNPs from a Japanese study reached P < 0.05.

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) examined the combined effects of SNCA, MAPT, GAK and HLA risk alleles. Compared with subjects carrying 0 or 1 risk allele, PD risk was doubled with 4 risk alleles (OR 2.49, P = 6.5 x 10(-8)) and 5-fold higher with 6 or more (OR 4.95, P = 5.5 x 10(-13)).

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Using NGRC data, Hamza et al. (2010) estimated that the heritability of PD declined from 0.6 to 0.4 after excluding known pathogenic and susceptibility loci, but stayed significant, suggesting that additional unidentified genes exist.

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) found that the frequency of the rs3129882 risk allele in controls varied significantly by region, from 0.36 in Washington to 0.46 in New York. It was low in subjects of Northern European ancestry and high in Southern Europeans, particularly Italians. Within each subpopulation, patients had a higher risk-allele frequency than controls.

subject: Hamza et al. (2010)
object: Hamza et al. (2010) noted that previous eQTL studies had identified rs3129882 as a cis-acting regulatory variant correlated with expression of HLA-DRA, HLA-DQA2 and HLA-DRB5. They suggested that the HLA association supports a role for neuroinflammation and immunity in PD pathogenesis.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset 50 years or younger), recruited at 13 movement disorders centers without regard to family history, for mutations in SNCA, PRKN, PINK1, DJ1, LRRK2, and GBA. They found mutations in 158 (16.6%): 64 (6.7%) in PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) in GBA, and 1 (0.2%) in DJ1. No carriers of the tested SNCA or PINK1 mutations were found.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Among the 953 patients with early-onset PD, Alcalay et al. (2010) identified 58 GBA mutation carriers: 18 L444P heterozygotes, 38 N370S heterozygotes, and 2 N370S homozygotes. GBA mutations accounted for 40% of all mutations detected. Carriers of GBA N370S were more likely to be Jewish than non-Jewish.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that, after adjustment for covariates, carrying GBA L444P was associated with a higher UPDRS-III motor score (worse motor performance) compared with non-carriers. They described this as the first report of a difference in motor severity between PD patients with different GBA mutations.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) identified 31 LRRK2 G2019S carriers (30 heterozygotes and 1 homozygote) and 1 carrier of the LRRK2 G2385R variant among patients with early-onset PD. G2019S carriers were more likely to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) motor phenotype (96%) and were more likely to be Jewish.

object: LRRK2

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that 33 patients were PRKN heterozygotes and 27 carried two PRKN mutations (homozygous or compound heterozygous). PRKN carriers had an earlier age at onset and were more often Hispanic (15.6% vs 5.9%). The authors suggested that the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the idea that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk factor for early-onset PD.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that mutations were more common in early-onset PD patients with onset at age 30 or younger (40.6% vs 14.6%), in those with Jewish ancestry (32.4% vs 13.7%), and in those with a first-degree family history of PD (23.9% vs 15.1%). The family-history association was absent in Jewish patients.

subject: Alcalay et al. (2010)
object: Alcalay et al. (2010) found 7 patients with early-onset PD who carried mutations in more than one gene, including LRRK2 G2019S together with GBA L444P or N370S, and PRKN heterozygous mutations together with GBA mutations. None of these patients reported PD in a first-degree relative.

subject: Corvol et al. (2011)
object: In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, Corvol et al. (2011) studied 33 Parkinson disease patients who were homozygous for the COMT Val158Met polymorphism: 17 were Val/Val (high activity, COMT-HH) and 16 were Met/Met (low activity, COMT-LL). Each patient had two acute levodopa challenges, one with 200 mg entacapone and one with placebo. Entacapone increased the best ON time more in COMT-HH than in COMT-LL patients (39 +/- 10 vs 9 +/- 9 minutes, p = 0.04). It also raised levodopa AUC more (+62% vs +34%, p = 0.01) and inhibited red blood cell COMT activity more in COMT-HH patients. The authors concluded that the COMT-HH genotype enhances the effect of entacapone on levodopa pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics.

subject: Mata et al. (2011)
object: Mata et al. (2011) genotyped 7 SNPs in 1,445 Parkinson disease patients and 1,161 controls from northern Spain. Under an additive model adjusted for sex, age and site, PD was significantly associated with rs356219 in SNCA (OR 1.23; 95% CI 1.09-1.38; p = 5.5 x 10(-4)) and with rs1800547 in MAPT (OR 0.79; 95% CI 0.70-0.90; p = 3.1 x 10(-4)). In age-stratified analyses, these associations were significant only in the late-onset group.

object: Mata et al. (2011) found that the A allele of MAPT rs1800547, a surrogate marker for the MAPT H1 haplotype, was associated with Parkinson disease under an adjusted dominant model in their Spanish case-control sample (OR 1.23; 95% CI 1.05-1.44; p = 1.1 x 10(-2)).

subject: Mata et al. (2011)
object: Mata et al. (2011) did not replicate the association of Parkinson disease with PARK16 (rs823156 near SLC41A1, p = 0.09; rs947211, p = 0.50), PARK17 (GAK rs11248051, p = 0.60), PARK18 (HLA-DRA rs3129882, OR 1.01, p = 0.88) or a chromosome 8 intergenic SNP among 1,445 Spanish patients and 1,161 controls. None of these markers was associated in the overall sample or in any age stratum. The authors suggested that population structure, insufficient power (particularly for PARK16), or population-specific environmental interactions could explain the discordance with earlier GWAS. For PARK18, their sample had 99% power at the originally reported OR of 1.31.

subject: Berman et al. (2011)
object: Berman et al. (2011) found that EAAC1 (SLC1A1)-null mice, which have impaired neuronal cysteine uptake and reduced neuronal glutathione, showed age-dependent loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, with no difference at 3 months but a 41 +/- 10% decrease by 12 months of age. Neuronal loss was accompanied by increased nitrotyrosine formation in nigral dopaminergic neurons, increased nitrosylated alpha-synuclein (primarily as dimers and higher-order aggregates), and microglial activation. Striatal dopamine and metabolites showed only nonsignificant reductions, and motor deficits were found only on the pole test at 12 months.

subject: Berman et al. (2011)
object: Berman et al. (2011) showed that oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a membrane-permeable cysteine prodrug, restored reactive thiol (glutathione) content in nigral dopaminergic neurons of EAAC1-null mice, and that long-term administration from weaning through 12 months reduced dopaminergic neuronal loss, nitrotyrosine immunoreactivity, and pole test deficits. The authors suggested that these findings provide a rationale for clinical evaluation of glutathione repletion in PD.

subject: Berman et al. (2011)
object: Berman et al. (2011) found that EAAC1 expression was higher on dopaminergic (TH-positive) neurons than on other neurons in mouse midbrain, and that normal human brain likewise showed increased EAAC1 expression in dopaminergic neurons; in 4 postmortem PD brains, the EAAC1 signal in surviving dopaminergic neurons was at least as great as in 4 control brains. They suggested a key role for EAAC1 in dopaminergic neuronal glutathione metabolism and a contributory role for glutathione depletion in dopaminergic neuronal death.

subject: Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011)
object: Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011) profiled miRNA expression in Parkinson disease brain samples. They found decreased miR-34b and miR-34c in brain areas with variable neuropathologic involvement at clinical (motor) Braak stages 4 and 5, including the amygdala, frontal cortex, substantia nigra, and cerebellum. The miR-34b/c changes were also present at pre-motor stages (Braak stages 1-3), in cases that had received no PD-related treatment during life.

subject: Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011)
object: In differentiated SH-SY5Y dopaminergic neuronal cells, Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011) found that depleting miR-34b or miR-34c moderately reduced cell viability. The depletion also altered mitochondrial function and dynamics, caused oxidative stress, and lowered total cellular ATP. Lower miR-34b/c was coupled to lower expression of DJ1 and Parkin, and both proteins were reduced in PD brain samples with strong miR-34b/c downregulation. The authors proposed that early miR-34b/c deregulation in PD triggers downstream transcriptome changes that underlie mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress.

subject: Chung et al. (2013)
object: Chung et al. (2013) made cortical neurons from iPS cells of a female Contursi kindred patient carrying the SNCA A53T mutation and from mutation-corrected isogenic controls. They identified pathologic phenotypes in the mutant neurons that were guided by modifiers from yeast alpha-synuclein toxicity screens. These phenotypes were increased nitric oxide and nitrosative stress (nitrotyrosine), accumulation of ER forms of the ERAD substrates glucocerebrosidase (GCase) and nicastrin starting at 4 weeks, and ER stress (increased PDI and BIP, with unchanged CHOP). Increased nitrotyrosine staining and accumulation of the ER form of GCase were also seen in postmortem cortex from A53T patients.

subject: Chung et al. (2013)
object: Chung et al. (2013) found that cortical neurons derived from iPS cells of a male Iowa kindred patient with SNCA triplication, who had aggressive dementia and parkinsonism, accumulated ERAD substrates and showed increased ER stress, closely phenocopying A53T neurons. Cortex from sporadic PD samples showed the same trend of ER GCase accumulation.

subject: Chung et al. (2013)
object: In a yeast alpha-synuclein toxicity model, Chung et al. (2013) found that alpha-synuclein caused dosage-dependent protein nitration that was specific to alpha-synuclein. Raising or lowering nitric oxide by deleting COX5 isoforms increased or decreased toxicity accordingly, showing that nitrosative stress contributes to toxicity. The yeast suppressor Hrd1 and its human homolog synoviolin (SYVN1) rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity in rat cortical neurons, and SYVN1 reduced ER accumulation of GCase and nicastrin in A53T patient neurons.

subject: Chung et al. (2013)
object: Chung et al. (2013) found that NAB2, a small molecule from a yeast screen that activates the Rsp5/Nedd4 ubiquitin ligase pathway, lowered nitric oxide levels in A53T patient neurons. It also increased the post-ER forms of nicastrin and GCase and decreased their immature forms. Lentiviral overexpression of NEDD4 had the same effect as the compound.

subject: Tardiff et al. (2013)
object: Tardiff et al. (2013) found an N-aryl benzimidazole (NAB) compound in a screen of yeast cells expressing toxic levels of α-synuclein. NAB reversed several α-synuclein-induced phenotypes: vesicular α-synuclein foci, reactive oxygen species, the block in ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and protein nitration. It did not reduce α-synuclein levels.

subject: Tardiff et al. (2013)
object: Tardiff et al. (2013) found that NAB reversed α-synuclein toxicity or pathology in three neuronal models: dopaminergic neuron degeneration in C. elegans expressing human α-synuclein, loss of dopaminergic neurons in rat primary cultures expressing A53T α-synuclein, and cortical neurons derived from induced pluripotent stem cells of PD patients carrying either the A53T mutation or an α-synuclein triplication. In the patient-derived neurons, both genotypes caused protein trafficking defects and nitrosative stress.

subject: Tardiff et al. (2013)
object: Tardiff et al. (2013) used chemical genetic screens in yeast to show that NAB acts through the HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, the yeast homolog of the mammalian Nedd4 family, to promote endosomal transport. A point mutation in Rsp5 (rsp5G747E) conferred resistance to NAB2 and blocked its rescue of α-synuclein toxicity. α-Synuclein itself impaired endosomal trafficking from the plasma membrane and Golgi to the vacuole, and NAB2 restored this trafficking. The authors suggested that dysfunctional vesicle trafficking is a druggable node in α-synuclein pathology.

subject: Dong et al. (2014)
object: Dong et al. (2014) tested 11 SNPs from earlier genomewide association studies (GWAS) of pigmentation or melanoma in the PAGE study (808 PD cases and 1,623 controls, all non-Hispanic white). They then tested 360 such SNPs in the IPDGC dataset (5,333 PD cases and 12,019 controls). In PAGE, rs4911414 at the ASIP gene was associated with PD after Bonferroni correction (p = 0.001), but it was not associated with PD in IPDGC (p = 0.43). None of the 360 SNPs were associated with PD risk after correction for multiple comparisons. The authors concluded that GWAS SNPs for pigmentation or melanoma were not significantly associated with PD risk.

subject: Dong et al. (2014)
object: Dong et al. (2014) found that MC1R rs1805007, which an earlier smaller study had associated with PD, was not significantly associated with PD in the IPDGC dataset (OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.94-1.19, P = 0.37).

object: MC1R

subject: Dong et al. (2014)
object: In the PAGE study, Dong et al. (2014) found first primary melanoma in 18 PD cases (2.2%) and 26 controls (1.6%), giving a nonsignificant odds ratio of 1.32 (95% CI 0.71-2.44). Hair, eye, and skin color were not significantly associated with PD risk.

subject: Raj et al. (2014)
object: Raj et al. (2014) carried out an eQTL study of purified naive CD4+ T cells and CD14+CD16- monocytes from 461 healthy individuals of European, African American, and East Asian ancestry in Boston. Susceptibility alleles for Parkinson disease and Alzheimer disease were enriched for monocyte-specific cis-eQTL effects. Alleles for autoimmune diseases such as multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis were instead enriched for T cell-specific effects. The authors suggested that the inflammatory component of susceptibility to neurodegenerative diseases may be driven more strongly by the myeloid compartment of the immune system.

subject: Raj et al. (2014)
object: Raj et al. (2014) noted that their study examined young, healthy individuals and so supported a role for myeloid cells in the prodromal phase of neurodegenerative diseases. They proposed that blood monocytes are likely proxies for infiltrating macrophages and/or resident microglia at the sites of neuropathology.

subject: Tell-Marti et al. (2015)
object: Tell-Marti et al. (2015) sequenced the entire MC1R gene in 870 Parkinson disease patients and 736 controls from Spain. They found that the MC1R melanoma risk variant p.R160W (rs1805008) was marginally associated with PD (odds ratio 2.10, gender- and age-adjusted p = 0.009, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.063). The authors suggested that MC1R genetic variants modulate the risk of PD in the Spanish population.

subject: MC1R p.R160W
object: MC1R

subject: Tell-Marti et al. (2015)
object: Tell-Marti et al. (2015) noted that epidemiologic studies have reported co-occurrence of Parkinson disease and melanoma, which prompted their study of MC1R, a gene whose common variants are associated with melanoma, as a modifier of PD risk.

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Sulzer et al. (2017) studied 67 patients with PD and 36 age-matched healthy controls from San Diego and New York City. About one-third of the PD patients carried the HLA class II alleles DRB1*15:01/DRB5*01:01, compared with about 15% of controls (p = 0.036 and 0.022), which the authors took as showing an association of HLA-DR variants with PD in their cohort.

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Sulzer et al. (2017) stimulated peripheral blood mononuclear cells with alpha-synuclein peptides and identified 2 antigenic regions. One was near the N terminus (residues 31-46, the Y39 region), and Y39 phosphorylation was not required for the response. The other was near the C terminus (residues 116-140, the S129 region) and required phosphorylation of S129, a form present in Lewy bodies. Phosphorylated S129 epitopes produced markedly higher IL-5 responses in PD patients than in controls (p = 0.02).

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that IFN-gamma and IL-5 responses to the Y39 and S129 region epitopes differed significantly between PD patients and controls. In PD patients the response was mainly IL-5 (71% IL-5 vs 29% IFN-gamma), whereas the rarer responses in controls were not polarized in this way. About 40% of PD participants had immune responses to alpha-synuclein epitopes.

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Using intracellular cytokine staining in 9 PD participants, Sulzer et al. (2017) found that about 0.2% of CD3+ T cells responded to alpha-synuclein peptides. The responses were mostly mediated by CD4+ T cells producing IL-4 or IFN-gamma; in 1 patient the response was mostly from IFN-gamma-producing CD8+ T cells. T-cell lines specific for these epitopes were also activated by antigen-presenting cells pulsed with native or fibrillized alpha-synuclein protein (in 7 of 12 and 11 of 12 cases, respectively).

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: In in vitro binding assays, Sulzer et al. (2017) found that the PD-associated HLA class II alleles DRB1*15:01 and DRB5*01:01 bound the Y39-region epitope with high affinity (2.8 nM and 8.1 nM). C-terminal S129-region peptides bound HLA class II alleles weakly, apart from 1 peptide that bound DQB1*05:01 strongly, which the authors suggested meant these peptides are recognized promiscuously. HLA expression did not differ between PD patients with and without DRB1*15:01, suggesting that the DRB1*15:01 association with PD is not due to differential expression of the protein.

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that among PD patients, responders to the Y39 epitope more often carried DRB1*15:01 (odds ratio 4.4), DRB5*01:01 (odds ratio 3.7), DQB1*03:04 and A*11:01 than non-responders. DRB3*02:02 was negatively associated with response, suggesting it might be protective. The 4 alleles DRB1*15:01, DRB5*01:01, DQB1*03:04 and A*11:01 together accounted for every individual responding to the Y39 epitope (p = 0.00007). About half of PD patients carried one of these 4 alleles, compared with about 20% of controls (p = 0.008).

subject: Sulzer et al. (2017)
object: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that 5 of 19 PD patients, but none of 12 controls, responded to short alpha-synuclein peptides that are candidates for MHC class I presentation. The 9-mer VLYVGSKTK (residues 37-45) bound HLA-A*11:01 with good affinity (IC50 = 161 nM), and responses to it were mostly from IFN-gamma-producing cells. The authors concluded that immune responses to alpha-synuclein in PD have both MHC class I- and class II-restricted components.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) screened 1,126 compounds for effects on endogenous SNCA expression in human SK-N-MC neuroblastoma cells. Three of the four confirmed hits were selective beta-2-adrenoreceptor (ADRB2) agonists: metaproterenol, clenbuterol, and salbutamol. Each lowered SNCA mRNA and alpha-synuclein protein in SK-N-MC cells and in rat primary cortical neurons.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) found that SNCA expression changed in both directions with beta-2-adrenoreceptor activity. Snca mRNA and protein rose by 100% and 120% in primary neurons from Adrb2-knockout mice. In SK-N-MC cells, silencing ADRB2 or treating with the antagonist propranolol increased SNCA expression, and overexpressing ADRB2 reduced it. ADRB2 was required for the agonist effect on SNCA.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) showed that beta-2-adrenoreceptor ligands regulate SNCA transcription through histone 3 lysine-27 acetylation (H3K27ac) at the SNCA promoter and at 2 putative enhancers in intron 4. Clenbuterol reduced H3K27ac at these sites, and propranolol increased it. Blocking deacetylation with valproic acid abolished the agonist effect. The authors proposed that beta-2-adrenoreceptor antagonists increase SNCA expression, leading to alpha-synuclein accumulation, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and increased PD risk.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) studied the whole Norwegian population (4.6 million people) using the Norwegian Prescription Database, with 11 years of follow-up. Use of the beta-2-adrenoreceptor agonist salbutamol was associated with a reduced risk of PD (rate ratio 0.66; 95% CI, 0.58-0.76), and the reduction was dose-dependent. Use of the antagonist propranolol was associated with an increased risk (rate ratio 2.20; 95% CI, 1.62-3.00). Inhaled corticosteroids did not reduce PD risk, which the authors took as evidence against smoking fully explaining the salbutamol association. The authors noted that association does not imply causation.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) found that intraperitoneal clenbuterol crossed the blood-brain barrier in wild-type mice and lowered alpha-synuclein protein and mRNA in the substantia nigra. Clenbuterol also prevented MPTP-induced loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons and cresyl violet-stained cells in the substantia nigra pars compacta.

subject: Mittal et al. (2017)
object: Mittal et al. (2017) used iPSC-derived neuronal precursor cells and neurons from a patient with autosomal dominant PD caused by SNCA locus triplication. Clenbuterol reduced SNCA mRNA and alpha-synuclein protein in these cells. Under rotenone exposure, it also reduced mitochondria-associated superoxide production and increased cell viability.
